Nicknamed the English Versailles, this residence was home to one of artist Antonio Canova’s famous statues of Hebe, the Greek goddess of youth. Van Cleef & Arpels pays tribute to this important work through the Dea Eterna clip. The piece depicts the goddess in [diamonds](https://katerinaperez.com/bucherer-inner-fire-diamond-high-jewellery-collection-review) and yellow gold, perched on a rough lapis lazuli and surrounded by a shimmering waterfall of marquise-cut diamonds and textured shards of yellow gold. A black pearl drop finishes the design, which is another nod to Hebe as it is a stone that symbolises eternal youth. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Dea Eterna clip in gold, white gold, rose gold, featuring a 3.47-ct oval-cut pink sapphire, blue sapphires, lapis lazuli, gray cultured pearl and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery Collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44214/VCA_Dea_Eterna_clip.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Dea Eterna clip in gold, white gold, rose gold, featuring a 3.47-ct oval-cut pink sapphire, blue sapphires, lapis lazuli, gray cultured pearl and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery Collection ### *Chapter II* – Paris The next stop along the Grand Route would be the capital of glamour, Paris. Travellers here would admire the works of art of the ‘Grand Siècle’, particularly those created under the reign of Louis XIV – the Sun King. In this chapter, the Van Cleef & Arpels’ designers honour the city’s penchant for ornate décor like bejewelled chandeliers and over-the-top fashion, using a palette of vivid colours mixed with bold geometric shapes. The Lucendi earrings evoke the beautiful wardrobe and opulence of the Parisian Court’s ladies-in-waiting. Rose [gold](https://katerinaperez.com/Black-Gold-Jewellery-Gallery), diamonds and pink sapphires create elaborate silhouettes that allude to the ornate and extravagant aesthetic of Versailles’ chandeliers. The focal point of each earring is an oval-cut rubellite, one weighing 11.48 and the other 10.14 carats. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Lucendi earrings in rose gold, white gold, two oval-cut rubellites weighing 11.48-cts and 10.14-cts, mauve sapphires and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44215/VCA_lucendi_earrings.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Lucendi earrings in rose gold, white gold, two oval-cut rubellites weighing 11.48-cts and 10.14-cts, mauve sapphires and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection This celebration of French fashion and taste is further seen in the Noeud Royal ring. This piece is a tribute to the impressive fashion scene born in Paris. A geometric bow of white gold set with baguette-cut and round brilliant diamonds culminates in a cushion-cut pink sapphire of 6.38 carats. The piece also honours the ribbon design motif – a key element in the Maison’s aesthetic since its creation. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Noeud Royal ring in white gold, featuring a 6.38-ct cushion-cut pink sapphire and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44216/VCA_Noeud_Royal_ring.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Noeud Royal ring in white gold, featuring a 6.38-ct cushion-cut pink sapphire and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ### *Chapter III* – The Alps Moving to a more natural landscape, the pieces in this third chapter celebrate the beautiful and untamed vegetation the Grand Tour pilgrims would have seen as they crossed the [Swiss Alps](https://katerinaperez.com/articles/House-of-Geneva-jewellery-jeweluxe-event-in-singapore). A drastic change from the fast-paced capital cities of London and Paris, the pieces in this section feature much cooler and softer-toned gemstones. The Regina Montium necklace considers the snow-capped mountains of Switzerland and its lush green forests. A frosted necklace composed of peaks of diamonds, tanzanite, aquamarines and violet sapphires slowly guides you towards an articulated centre piece, where two large cushion-cut tourmalines are nestled in a frame created from these same gems. The smaller 16.26-carat tourmaline sits at the heart of the necklace, whilst the larger 27.70-carat gem is detachable and can be worn as a pendant. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44276/VCA_Regina_Montium_necklace_model.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44279/VCA_Regina_Montium_necklace.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44232/Grand_Tour_COLLECTION_VCA.jpg) Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

The Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace can also be worn as a chocker without the detachable 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44278/Van_Cleef_Regina_Montium_necklace.jpg) The Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace can also be worn as a chocker without the detachable 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline ![

Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44231/VCA_Grand_Tour.jpg) Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Regina Montium transformable necklace in white gold, featuring a 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline, a 16.26-ct cushion-cut blue-green tourmaline, sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

The detachable 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline from the Regina Montium transformable necklace can be worn as a pendant

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44277/Regina_Montium_necklace_VCA.jpg) The detachable 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline from the Regina Montium transformable necklace can be worn as a pendant Another work of art inspired by mother nature that is celebrated in this chapter is the Edelweiss, the official flower of Switzerland. This wild plant that only blossoms at high altitudes is recreated as another celebrated Van Cleef & Arpels clip in white and intense yellow diamonds complemented by gentle blue sapphires. Close groups of yellow diamonds are set at the centre of the petals created from pear-shaped, square and marquise-cut white diamonds set in yellow and white gold to simultaneously bring a glacial feel to the design while complementing the colour of the warm yellow diamonds. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Étoile des Glaciers clip in gold, white gold, sapphires, white and yellow diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44280/Van_Cleef___Arpels_clip.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Étoile des Glaciers clip in gold, white gold, sapphires, white and yellow diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ### *Chapter IV* – Venice We next follow our Grand Tour journeymen across the mountains to the antique and renaissance treasures of Italy, where the first city they would reach is [Venice](https://katerinaperez.com/articles/Katerina-perez-red-carpet-venice-film-festival-2022). The pieces in this chapter reflect the waterfront gothic architecture of the city’s bridges, canals and piazzas. The Chant des Gondoliers necklace is a bejewelled model of the city’s canals and archways. Articulated pendeloques of white and yellow gold set with diamonds and deep blue sapphires create an arch motif, indicative of the city’s low bridges. Beneath each carved arch is a cabochon turquoise, of which there are sixteen in total. The seamless bold form of each stone evokes sun-lit blue waters that rush through the city’s canals, whilst the back of the necklace is set with a gradation of sapphires, conjuring the image of the shaded waters beneath each archway. This detailed backing is a telling design detail of Van Cleef & Arpels, where each high jewellery piece is perfectly polished and designed from back to front. The matching drop earrings are fashioned as individual segments of the necklace, each with its cabochon turquoise. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44287/Van_Cleef___Arpels_Chant_des_Gondoliers_necklace.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44236/VCA_Chant_des_Gondoliers.jpg) Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44237/Chant_des_Gondoliers_necklace.jpg) Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers necklace in gold, white gold, sapphires, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection Another important architectural monument in Venice is its best-known square – the Piazza San Marco. This is portrayed by the Reine de l’Adriatique necklace and its matching clip. It is a graphic set of jewels created with intense blue stones, diamonds and rose gold in the image of the Gothic architecture of St Mark’s Basilica. The openwork of the gold and gemstones on the necklace creates an almost mosaic effect that guides the eye to the oval-cut 9.40-carat sapphire at the pendant’s centre. The matching [clip](https://katerinaperez.com/iconic-famous-british-jewellers-1960s-60s) depicts the landscape of Venice seen from the sea in the form of a micro mosaic of gems. This piece can be detached and replaced with the brooch, creating two different necklaces and aesthetics. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Reine de L’Adriatique necklace and clip with interchangeable motifs in white gold, rose gold, a 9.40-ct oval-cut sapphire, sapphires, lapis lazuli, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44219/Reine_de_l_Adriatique_necklace.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Reine de L’Adriatique necklace and clip with interchangeable motifs in white gold, rose gold, a 9.40-ct oval-cut sapphire, sapphires, lapis lazuli, turquoise and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ### *Chapter V* – Florence Moving further into Italy, the pieces in this fifth chapter were created as a tribute to Florence as a place of romance and as the home of the [Renaissance](https://katerinaperez.com/best-charm-jewellery-bracelets-pendants-renaissance) movement. They shine a light on the remarkable painters of this artistic period. The Ode à l’Amour ring is instantly recognisable as a high jewellery interpretation of Sandro Botticelli’s masterpiece – The Birth of Venus. Through a blend of creativity and savoir-faire, a carved pink gold shell outlined with a brilliant diamond pave sits atop a white gold band. Inside the shell, Botticelli’s Venus takes the form of a beautiful oval-cut pink sapphire of 4.04 carats, surrounded by smaller pink sapphires, rubies, and diamonds. The curved shape of the shell particularly highlights the savoir-faire of the Maison. To replicate such a realistic shape, the in-house craftsmen employed ramolayé, where the rose gold is carved before being raised in volume. This allows for a shell of striking three-dimensional shape and texture. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Ode à l’Amour ring in rose gold, white gold, a 4.04-ct oval-cut pink sapphire, rubies, pink sapphires and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44220/Ode___l_amour_ring_-_Beauty_Packshot___Van_Cleef___Arpels_SA_-_2023.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Ode à l’Amour ring in rose gold, white gold, a 4.04-ct oval-cut pink sapphire, rubies, pink sapphires and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection Another important Florentine painter honoured in this chapter is Angelo di Cosimo, more commonly known as Bronzino. This Florentine artist was famed for his representation of pearls in his works, as most of his female portrait subjects are seen wearing pearl earrings, chokers or decorative headpieces. The Perla di Angelo necklace pays tribute to this jewellery detail in the master’s works by creating a necklace composed of yellow gold, 30.11 carats of emerald-cut emeralds and fourteen white natural pearls. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace in gold, white gold, emerald-cut emeralds, white natural pearls and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44283/VCA_Perla_di_Angelo_emerald_necklace.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace in gold, white gold, emerald-cut emeralds, white natural pearls and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace in gold, white gold, emerald-cut emeralds, white natural pearls and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44239/Perla_di_Angelo_Van_Cleef_necklace.jpg) Making of the Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace in gold, white gold, emerald-cut emeralds, white natural pearls and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ![

The Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace features 18.60-cts of white natural pearls

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44240/VCA_Perla_di_Angelo.jpg) The Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace features 18.60-cts of white natural pearls ![

The Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace features 30.11-cts of emerald-cut emeralds

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44242/Perla_di_Angelo_emerald_necklace.jpg) The Van Cleef & Arpels Perla di Angelo necklace features 30.11-cts of emerald-cut emeralds ### *Chapter VI* – Rome Arriving in Rome, the educational focus of the travellers would be the historical importance of the city and the relics of ancient civilisations that can be found throughout its cityscape. The pieces in this chapter shed light on the antiquity of this important place and its imperial [history](https://katerinaperez.com/toi-first-emirati-fine-jewellery-brand-cannes-film-festival-red-carpet) by featuring gems emblazoned with reminders of the city’s global impact. The city’s great ancient emperors and civilisations are captured in three sculptural clips featuring a glyptic gemstone. This craft was popular during antiquity and involved carving designs and shapes on the surface of gems or completely transforming their shape to depict figures or symbols. The carved gemstones originate from the first to third centuries, each of which is a historical artefact in itself. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Laurier Impérial, Anfora and Fresque Céleste clips from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44221/Laurier_Imperial__Anfora___Fresque_Celeste_Clips.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Laurier Impérial, Anfora and Fresque Céleste clips from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection The first clip in this series is a sapphire engraved with a bust of the emperor Caracalla, famed for Roman baths. He is depicted in profile, dressed in a traditional robe adorned with fibula. This gem is set in the Laurier Impérial clip, shaped like the laurel wreath crowns that Roman emperors wore. ![

Van Cleep & Arpels Laurier Impérial clip in gold, white gold, a 4.90-ct carved cushion-cut sapphire, sapphires, lapis lazuli and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44222/Laurier_Clip.jpg) Van Cleep & Arpels Laurier Impérial clip in gold, white gold, a 4.90-ct carved cushion-cut sapphire, sapphires, lapis lazuli and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection The second carved stone in this series is a red jasper intaglio that dates to the 2nd century and is engraved with an amphora motif, a traditional ancient Greek two-handed clay vase. The stone is set against a gold and diamond-textured reiteration of the vase, alongside lapis lazuli cabochons and an oval-cut spessartite garnet weighing 4.87 carats. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Anfora clip in gold, rose gold, a 3.47-ct carved red jasper motif, a 4.87-ct oval-cut spessartite garnet, lapis lazuli and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44223/Anfora_clip_-_Beauty_Packshot_l%CC%A7_Van_Cleef___Arpels_SA_-_2023.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Anfora clip in gold, rose gold, a 3.47-ct carved red jasper motif, a 4.87-ct oval-cut spessartite garnet, lapis lazuli and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection The final gem in this series of three clips is an 8.62-carat [citrine](https://katerinaperez.com/10-things-you-need-to-know-about-citrine) cabochon engraved with a crescent moon and stars. This intaglio was produced between the 1st and 2nd centuries and is set against a backdrop of a carved gold and diamond night sky, further highlighting the magnificent carving of this ancient stone. What is particularly interesting about this final gem is that citrine was rarely used in the history of glyptic art. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Fresque Céleste clip in gold, white gold, a 8.62-ct carved cabochon-cut citrine and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

](https://www.katerinaperez.com/uploads/editor_file/link/44224/Laurier_Imperial__Anfora___Fresque_Celeste_Clips-1.jpg) Van Cleef & Arpels Fresque Céleste clip in gold, white gold, a 8.62-ct carved cabochon-cut citrine and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection ### *Chapter VII* – Naples After the eternal city, the Grand Tour would move south to Naples, where they would experience a more rugged and exotic landscape of vibrant colours. The Maison chose to honour the tropical flora surrounding the Gulf of Naples. Inspired by the hanging gardens of Ravello and the Amalfi Coast, the Maison presents a set of clips filled with green foliage and colourful flowers. The Symphonie Florale clip recreates the atmosphere of strolling through the vegetation of an [Italian](https://katerinaperez.com/pomellato-ode-to-milan-high-jewellery-collection-review) villa’s garden. An 8.10-carat spessartite garnet, a 7.01-carat tsavorite garnet and a 7.31-carat pink garnet are set in swirls of white and rose gold mixed with green tsavorites and mauve sapphires. The Symphonie Végétale clip evokes a similar vision. An oval-cut pink tourmaline sits at the centre of a blooming floral shape created from white and rose gold, coloured sapphires and white diamonds. Finally, the Symphonie de l’Eau clip is inspired by the Gulf itself. The reflections of its colourful landscape in the water are brought to light through a 5.88-carat cabochon black opal with intense fires. The gem is set in a leaf-like shape designed in white and rose gold set with sapphires, tsavorite, garnets, green tourmalines and diamonds. ![

Van Cleef & Arpels Symphonie Florale clip in white gold, rose gold, a 8.10-ct oval-cut spessartite garnet, a 7.01-ct oval-cut tsavorite garnet, a 7.31-ct oval-cut pink garnet, tsavorites, spessartite garnets, mauve sapphires and diamonds from Le Grand Tour High Jewellery collection

This article from KaterinaPerez.com (published August 18, 2023, by Livia Primo Lack) provides an in-depth review of Van Cleef & Arpels' "Le Grand Tour" high jewellery collection. The collection is an ode to the popular 18th-century European voyage undertaken by the enlightened aristocracy, consisting of 70 pieces that reinterpret the works of art, flora, architectural details, and historical monuments of the most popular cities visited during the Grand Tour. The collection was presented at L'École des Arts Joailliers on Place Vendôme in a classroom setting, underscoring the educational purpose of these historic journeys. The collection is divided into eight chapters named after key stops along the Grand Tour route, each celebrating a different city or region:

Chapter I – London: Pays homage to Wedgewood porcelain with white and blue gemstone combinations. Key pieces include the Josiah transformable necklace (two oval-cut Sri Lankan sapphires of 25.10 and 21.78 carats that can detach to become earrings) and the Dea Eterna clip (inspired by Antonio Canova's statue of Hebe at Chatsworth House, featuring a 3.47-ct pink sapphire, lapis lazuli, gray cultured pearl, and a black pearl drop symbolizing eternal youth).

Chapter II – Paris: Honours the ornate décor of the Grand Siècle under Louis XIV. The Lucendi earrings feature oval-cut rubellites of 11.48 and 10.14 carats with rose gold and pink sapphires, while the Noeud Royal ring features a 6.38-ct cushion-cut pink sapphire in a geometric bow design.

Chapter III – The Alps: Celebrates Swiss alpine vegetation with cooler, softer-toned gemstones. The Regina Montium transformable necklace features a detachable 27.70-ct oval-cut blue-green tourmaline (worn as a pendant) and a 16.26-ct cushion-cut tourmaline, along with sapphires, aquamarines, tanzanites, and diamonds. The Étoile des Glaciers clip recreates the Edelweiss flower (Switzerland's official flower) in white and yellow diamonds with blue sapphires.

Chapter IV – Venice: Reflects waterfront gothic architecture. The Chant des Gondoliers necklace features articulated arch motifs with sixteen cabochon turquoise stones and a detailed sapphire-graded backing. The Reine de l'Adriatique necklace (depicting Piazza San Marco and St Mark's Basilica) features a 9.40-ct oval-cut sapphire, with an interchangeable clip/brooch that creates two different necklace aesthetics.

Chapter V – Florence: Tributes the Renaissance movement. The Ode à l'Amour ring is a high jewellery interpretation of Botticelli's "The Birth of Venus," featuring a carved pink gold shell (created using the ramolayé technique) with a 4.04-ct oval-cut pink sapphire. The Perla di Angelo necklace honours painter Bronzino's representation of pearls, featuring yellow gold, 30.11 carats of emerald-cut emeralds, and fourteen white natural pearls (18.60 cts).

Chapter VI – Rome: Features three sculptural clips incorporating genuine ancient glyptic gemstones (carved stones from the 1st to 3rd centuries). The Laurier Impérial clip features a 4.90-ct carved cushion-cut sapphire engraved with a bust of Emperor Caracalla. The Anfora clip features a 2nd-century red jasper intaglio with an amphora motif alongside a 4.87-ct spessartite garnet. The Fresque Céleste clip features an 8.62-ct citrine cabochon engraved with a crescent moon and stars (notable because citrine was rarely used in glyptic art).

Chapter VII – Naples: Celebrates the tropical flora of the Gulf of Naples, inspired by the hanging gardens of Ravello and the Amalfi Coast. The Symphonie Florale clip features an 8.10-ct spessartite garnet, 7.01-ct tsavorite garnet, and 7.31-ct pink garnet. The Symphonie Végétale clip features a 4.81-ct oval-cut pink tourmaline. The Symphonie de l'Eau clip features a 5.88-ct cabochon black opal set in a leaf-like design.

Chapter VIII – Baden-Baden: The final stop honours the German spa town's timbered frame houses and ivy-covered walls. The Jeu de Colombage transformable ring features a 13.35-ct sugar loaf Colombian emerald with rubies, sapphires, and diamonds, and can be worn in four different ways.

The article concludes that Le Grand Tour is Van Cleef & Arpels' most historically inspired collection to date, with each jewel containing hidden meanings and symbols that take the viewer on an educational journey. Key materials used throughout include turquoise, tourmaline, sapphire, rubellite, pearl, opal, lapis lazuli, intaglio, garnet, emerald, and citrine.

# Le Grand Tour by Van Cleef & Arpels

Sep 27, 2023

##### July 2023. Walking through the heavy door separating me from a noisy Parisian street to admire the latest high jewellery collection from [Van Cleef & Arpels](https://legemmologue.com/2022/07/08/legend-of-diamonds-par-van-cleef-arpels/) can only mean one thing: amazement. A few minutes later, as the pieces were unveiled, there was no doubt that the jewellery house had just signed a magnificent collection in which the great cities of Europe had become jewellery prodigies. The Grand Tour by Van Cleef & Arpels is nothing but diamonds, multicoloured stones and blooming flowers on jewellery sets with multiple wearings.

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/7-1024x1024.jpg)

Symphonie florale clip. White gold, pink gold, an oval spessartite garnet of 8.10 carats, an oval pink garnet of 7.31 carats, an oval tsavorite garnet of 7.01 carats, purple sapphires, tsavorite and spessartite garnets, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/9-1024x1024.jpg)

Brooch in pink gold, white gold, diamonds, garnets, zircons and opals. van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

![le grand tour van cleef & arpels](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/10-1024x1024.jpg)

Brooch in pink gold, white gold, diamonds, pink and violet sapphires. van Cleef & Arpels **SA** – 2023

## 1- The Grand Tour, a voyage of initiation

The “birth” of the Grand Tour is usually attributed to England in the sixteenth century. But in reality, the historical traces of this great voyage of initiation go back much further. From the 11th century onwards, the Middle Ages, with the Gregorian reform, saw the emergence of monastic and cathedral schools that would gradually give shape to the great European universities. The *Schola Medica Salernitana* was founded in the 10th century, the University of Bologna in 1088 and Oxford in 1116.

Reserved for the clergy (many of whom were members of the nobility), these schools were part of a political context of relative stability in Europe, which paved the way for greater geographical mobility and saw the establishment of the practice of an academic tour, also known as *peregrinatio academica*, which consisted of studying at other universities to enrich one’s culture. This notion will inevitably bring to mind the current Erasmus programme (created in 1987), which will bring back memories for many of you. But the abandonment of Latin is gradually signalling the end of this medieval practice.

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/15-1024x1024.jpg)

Boboli ring. White gold, one 9.25 ct emerald-cut emerald, emeralds, diamonds  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2021

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/12-1024x1024.jpg)

Ode to love ring. Pink gold, white gold, one 4.04 carat oval pink sapphire (Madagascar), rubies, pink sapphires, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/13-1024x1024.jpg)

Rose Garden ring. Pink gold, an emerald-cut pink tourmaline of 23.67 carats, coloured sapphires, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2022

Back in the 16th century, this travel system reappeared. Reserved for aristocratic youth, this two- to three-year tour of Europe’s major cities became a compulsory part of their training before they entered the world. Its purpose: to enrich their general culture, perfect their political education, develop their knowledge of foreign languages and their sexual education. But we mustn’t forget its ultimate goal, with its undeniable social function. By taking this trip, young men created shared memories and affirmed their financial position. By visiting what had to be seen, the trip helped to strengthen the social ties between families. Back in 2023, there was nothing better than a [school](https://www.lecolevancleefarpels.com/fr/fr?mid=2300tef18521&mkwid=sPlyHRCvi_dc&pcrid=564224902228&kword=ecole des arts joailliers&match=p&plid=&gad=1&gclid=Cj0KCQjwvL-oBhCxARIsAHkOiu1Q79YzTxQGFbVUKLwlIxP1IG7h_eM2uq7eTJ4LWkHxP2OioW7j0AoaAl_vEALw_wcB&gclsrc=aw.ds) to present this new collection!

## 2- London, Paris, Baden-Baden, Venice, Rome… in any order you like

Although the original journey did not follow a precise itinerary, in the version standardised by the English, you have to leave London and go to France. Next, the Alps, the striking landscapes of Baden-Württemberg and Switzerland, then Italy, its ancient ruins, its paintings, its gentle way of life…

At Van Cleef & Arpels, the Grand Tour comprises almost 70 pieces showcasing the major stages of this journey. Admire the earthenware for which London is famous and visit Chatsworth House, nicknamed the English Versailles, the sumptuous residence of the Dukes of Devonshire. France offers the legacy of the Sun King, its effervescence and its French-style gardens, whose influences can be found in Italy.

But for that, you have to cross the Alps, stop off in Switzerland, admire the lakes and mountains, lose yourself in the wilderness and learn about edelweiss, a mysterious flower that is not easy to capture. Finally, there’s Venice, Rome, Naples and Florence, with the cries of the gondoliers, the ancient remains around every corner, the painters’ studios and the great names in painting, such as Botticelli.

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/14-1024x1024.jpg)

© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/11-1024x1024.jpg)

Schäppel ring. Pink gold, white gold, a 3.28 carat cushion ruby (Burma), emeralds, rubies, pink and yellow sapphires, spessartite garnets, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2021

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/8-1024x1024.jpg)

Imperial laurel clip. White gold, yellow gold, an intaglio engraved cushion sapphire weighing 4.90 carats (Sri Lanka), sapphires, lapis lazuli, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

![](https://legemmologue.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/09/6-1024x1024.jpg)

Anfora clip. Yellow gold, pink gold, an intaglio engraved red jasper motif, an oval spessartite garnet of 4.87 carats, lapis lazuli, diamonds.  
© Van Cleef & Arpels SA – 2023

Italy is the major chapter in this new collection. It infuses each bracelet, each necklace. Here the Piazza Divina in Rome, there Etruscan inspirations, elsewhere Saint Mark’s Square… But nature is also called upon. An eternal inspiration for jewellers, it is constantly reinventing itself, giving rise here to brooches with dense foliage, but also to a jewellery translation of the trees in the garden of Lichtenthal Abbey. Certainly my favourite pieces in this new opus.

The stones are fabulous, and bear witness to the privileged links that unite the House with the highest-quality suppliers. As for the care taken in selecting the raw materials, it is indissociable from the many skills that are setting Van Cleef & Arpels ever higher in the [jewellery constellations](https://legemmologue.com/2022/09/06/la-petite-histoire-de-la-joaillerie-celeste-et-spatiale/).

This webpage is an article from "Le Gemmologue," a jewelry-focused blog written by Marie Chabrol (speaker, consultant, and teacher), published on September 27, 2023. The article reviews "Le Grand Tour by Van Cleef & Arpels," the jewelry house's latest high jewellery collection inspired by the historical European "Grand Tour" travel tradition.

Key content:
- The collection comprises nearly 70 pieces featuring diamonds, multicolored stones, and floral motifs with multiple-wearing designs, showcasing major European cities as jewelry inspirations.
- The historical Grand Tour originated as a medieval academic practice (*peregrinatio academica*) — studying at different European universities — before reappearing in the 16th century as a two-to-three-year compulsory journey for aristocratic youth through Europe's major cities to enrich their culture, political education, and language skills, while strengthening social ties between families.
- The collection's itinerary spans London (earthenware, Chatsworth House), France (Sun King legacy, French-style gardens), Switzerland/Baden-Baden (lakes, mountains, edelweiss), and Italy (Venice, Rome, Naples, Florence) — with Italy being the "major chapter" of the collection, featuring inspirations like Piazza Divina in Rome, Etruscan motifs, Saint Mark's Square, and foliage brooches inspired by the gardens of Lichtenthal Abbey.
- Notable pieces described include: Symphonie florale clip (with spessartite, pink, and tsavorite garnets), Boboli ring (9.25 ct emerald-cut emerald), Ode to love ring (4.04 carat oval pink sapphire from Madagascar), Rose Garden ring (23.67 carats emerald-cut pink tourmaline), Jeu de colombage transformable ring (13.35-carat sugarloaf emerald from Colombia), Schäppel ring (3.28 carat cushion ruby from Burma), Imperial laurel clip (4.90 carat intaglio engraved cushion sapphire from Sri Lanka), and Anfora clip (intaglio engraved red jasper with 4.87 carat spessartite garnet).
- The author praises the collection's exceptional stones, which reflect the House's privileged relationships with high-quality suppliers, and its combination of craftsmanship skills.

# Treasured Travels: Van Cleef & Arpels Launches Le Grand Tour Collection

* [Text by Kate Missine](https://magnifissance.com/author/kate/)
* Photos Courtesy of  Van Cleef & Arpels

Updated on June 24, 2025

Share on facebook

Share on pinterest

Share on email

Share on twitter

The art, architecture, and storied history of Europe’s most famous cities have long been a boundless source of design inspiration. [Van Cleef & Arpels](https://magnifissance.com/?s=Van+Cleef+%26+Arpels&ee_search_query=&subscribe=)’s new *Le Grand Tour* [high jewellery](https://magnifissance.com/?s=high+jewellery&ee_search_query=&subscribe=) collection continues this tradition by embarking on a historical journey through Europe’s cultural heart.

[![van-cleef-9](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://magnifissance.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/van-cleef-9.jpg)

*The Fleuve De Glace pearl sautoir necklace. Photo by Marc de Groot*

“At the beginning of the 20th century, when [Van Cleef & Arpels](http://www.vancleefarpels.com) was founded, curiosity for other cultures, periods, and forms of art was a way to fuel one’s imagination and give rise to innovative creations. We followed the trail of our predecessors and chose cities that were renowned stops historically,” says Nicolas Bos, the brand’s president and CEO.

Making their way through London, Paris, Rome, Venice, the Alps, and other birthplaces of European culture, the collection’s pieces act as precious souvenirs by honouring each of the Grand Tour’s stops.

One of the primary sources of inspiration, according to Bos, is the antique jewellery style unique to each region—Roman, Etruscan, Medieval, or Renaissance—combined with the jeweller’s own legacy of craftsmanship.

[![van-cleef-8](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://magnifissance.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/van-cleef-8.jpg)

*Top: The Anfora clip reveals the red jasper intaglio stone: a gem that stands out for its historical value. Bottom: The Dea Eterna clip in gold, white gold, and rose gold, featuring a 3.47-carat oval-cut pink sapphire, blue sapphires, lapis lazuli, gray cultured pearl, and diamonds. Photos by Inès Dieleman*

The Grand Tour adventure begins in London, with a sculptural diamond and lapis lazuli clip taking cue from Chatsworth House, the opulent residence of the Duke of Devonshire. From there, it’s off to 18th-century Paris, with rose gold chain earrings evoking the chandeliers in the boudoirs of the royal ladies-in-waiting.

[![van-cleef-6](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://magnifissance.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/van-cleef-6.jpg)

*Left: Suggesting the elaborate silhouette of 18th-century chandeliers, the Lucendi earrings are suspended by a chain from a triple loop of rose gold. Right: The Étoile des Glaciers clip in gold, white gold, sapphires, white, and yellow diamonds.*

The Alps give inspiration both to a tourmaline necklace that recalls the cold beauty of ice caves and to a flower clip evoking blooming meadows. A romp through the landmarks of Italy brings forth a jewelled clip inspired by the horn of plenty of ancient Rome, while the Chant des gondoliers necklace and earrings speak to the enchanting Venetian canals.

[![van-cleef-11](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://magnifissance.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/van-cleef-11.jpg)

*Top: The Piazza Divina necklace borrowed the geometry of Bernini’s baroque architecture and enhanced it with the green emerald detachable medallion. Bottom: Elizabeth earrings with detachable pendants, Cornucopia clip, and Schäppel ring. Photos by Marc de Groot*

Of special significance are the landscape bracelets—a nod to watercolour paintings in journals and travel books that transport the wearer from one scene to another. In the words of Bos, the resulting lineup creates “a colourful sketchbook that invites us to dive into destinations and gemstones.”

[![VCA Toronto Bloor](data:image/gif;base64,R0lGODlhAQABAAAAACH5BAEKAAEALAAAAAABAAEAAAICTAEAOw==)](https://magnifissance.com/wp-content/uploads/2024/01/van-cleef-12.jpg)

*Van Cleef & Arpels’s newly opened Canadian flagship boutique on Toronto’s Bloor Street.*

Van Cleef & Arpels also recently opened the doors to its first flagship store in Canada. With a design inspired by a Parisian apartment, the 2,500-square-foot boutique on Toronto’s Bloor Street marks an important step in the brand’s evolution in North America.

The collection draws inspiration from antique jewellery styles unique to each region—Roman, Etruscan, Medieval, and Renaissance—combined with the jeweller's own craftsmanship legacy. Key pieces include: a diamond and lapis lazuli clip inspired by Chatsworth House in London; rose gold chain earrings evoking 18th-century Parisian chandeliers; a tourmaline necklace inspired by ice caves in the Alps; a flower clip evoking blooming meadows; a jewelled clip inspired by ancient Rome's horn of plenty; and the Chant des gondoliers necklace and earrings inspired by Venetian canals. The collection also features "landscape bracelets" that nod to watercolour paintings in journals and travel books. Additionally, the article notes that Van Cleef & Arpels recently opened its first flagship store in Canada—a 2,500-square-foot boutique on Toronto's Bloor Street designed to resemble a Parisian apartment. The article includes quotes from Nicolas Bos, the brand's president and CEO, about the collection's inspiration and significance. It is part of Magnifissance's "Inspired for a Beautiful Life" publication.

# How Van Cleef & Arpels Turned the Grand Tour Into a Sumptuous High Jewelry Collection

## The upper-crust travel tradition informed a suite of stunning creations, each more worldly than the next.

#### [Paige Reddinger](https://robbreport.com/author/paige-reddinger/)

Deputy Editor, Watch & Jewelry Editor

#### Paige Reddinger's Most Recent Stories

![Van Cleef & Arpels Chant des Gondoliers Necklace](https://robbreport.com/wp-content/uploads/2023/11/JH013497_-_Chant_des_gondoliers_necklace-1.jpg?w=1000)

Stilt-walking harlequins, leaping court jesters, gladiators, riders on horseback, harem girls, and more descended upon the courtyard followed by a gilded carriage carrying five statuesque ladies dripping in jewels. This was the setting for one of the year’s more spectacular high-[jewelry](https://robbreport.com/tag/jewelry/) reveals, courtesy of [Van Cleef & Arpels](https://www.vancleefarpels.com/). The Cirque du Soleil–level performance in the gardens of Rome’s Villa Medici (now home to the French Academy) brought to life the building’s 19th-century Louis Dupré painting *Châteaubriand reçoit la grande-duchesse Hélène de Russie dans les jardins de la Villa Médicis le 29 avril 1829.* It was followed by a dinner at an outdoor pavilion on the property, where guests were serenaded by an opera singer, suspended from a series of lit balloons, who floated on the gardens’ horizon.

### Related Stories

* [Glashütte Original’s New Chronographs Take Cues From Horological History](https://robbreport.com/style/watch-collector/glashutte-original-senator-chronograph-watches-1238568038/)
* [Rolex’s Certified Pre-Owned Business Is Booming](https://robbreport.com/style/watch-collector/rolex-certified-pre-owned-business-boom-1238567194/)
* [Nicolas Ghesquière and Pat McGrath Teamed up on Louis Vuitton’s First Beauty Collab](https://robbreport.com/style/grooming/la-beaute-louis-vuitton-makeup-collab-1238568915/)

### Related Stories

![The reenactment at the Villa Medici in Rome for Van Cleef’s high-jewelry reveal.](https://robbreport.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-robbreport-2017-v2/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

All of this was put on to show off the opulent jewels inspired by the Grand Tour, a custom dating back to the 16th century in which upper-class Europeans traveled the continent to study art, literature, architecture, music, and more as a sort of extended (and lavish) cultural boot camp. The pieces in the collection all correspond to a leg of the journey—including London, Paris, the Alps, and Venice. Take, for example, this white- and rose-gold Fleuve de glace (“ice river”) necklace with a 48.8-carat cushion-cut green beryl meant to represent the hues of the Grindelwald Glacier, in the Swiss Alps, as well as the colors used in the works of Swiss landscape painters Caspar Wolf and Samuel Birmann. It also comes with a 4.17-carat cushion-cut pink spinel and 288 blue-tourmaline beads totaling 157.09 carats, plus emeralds, pink sapphires, gray cultured pearls, and diamonds.

![Van Cleef & Arpels’s Fleuve de glace necklace](https://robbreport.com/wp-content/themes/pmc-robbreport-2017-v2/assets/public/lazyload-fallback.gif)

“The idea is to never go too academic but to also offer our guests an invitation to discover some elements of art and culture that we feel are inspiring,” says Van Cleef & Arpels president and CEO Nicolas Bos. “And then, of course, our job is to translate this into jewels that stand by themselves, and I hope are nice pieces of jewelry, but are also an interpretation of this story.”

# [Bulgari Launches Mediterranea High Jewelry and Watches Collection in Venice 2023](/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

 /   [Anne Enke](/jewelry-news?author=55f45171e4b0df69cc0c28ee)  

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/ebbc0fb9-96ff-4654-a380-ac8b43782af1/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00005.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

## **Bulgari *Mediterranea***

Bulgari chose Venice to host the unveiling of its new High-Jewelry and high-End Watch collection *Mediterranea*. The choice of La Serenissima [Italian name for the Republic of Venice] references the Byzantine title that governed the city’s role as a center of trade and business.

These Bulgari Mediterranea images were shot by photographer **Gregoire Alexandre** [[IG](https://www.instagram.com/p/CsTI29zACeY/?hl=en)] for **V Magazine**, [who shares their thoughts](https://vmagazine.com/article/eternal-jewelry-eternal-city-with-bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry/) about the collection.

Venice was also a city that preferred conflict mediation and peaceful solutions that arose with the many diverse cultures and peoples navigating the Mediterranean Sea in pursuit of commercial trading partners and sometimes territorial conquest.

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/f9887adb-6967-43ce-a7ba-87ed68336d40/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00001.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

## **Venice Crossroads**

For centuries, Venice existed as a symbol of openness to different cultures, bringing together distant universes and creative inspirations. Historical scholars, anthropologists and inquisitive lay people like **Anne of Carversville** understand that Venice existed as an exciting beacon of human possibility built on cultural diversity, artistry and ideas.

LVMH-owned Bulgari retraces this imaginary trip across the Mediterranean Sea as an inexhaustible source of inspiration layering multiple arts, traditions and crafts into its newest High-Jewelry collection.

> *“This High Jewelry collection is an homage to the Mediterranean beauty and essence in all its forms. For me, being in the Mediterranean region is an awakening of all senses, and a real inspirational experience. The architecture, the nature, the people, I am eyeing beauty everywhere. Is an inspiring melting pot, where many different cultures and societies have mingled and enriched each other over centuries. Our hospitality and open-mindedness are rooted in this history.” — Lucia Silvestri Bulgari Jewelry Creative Director*

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/60587de4-dd33-468f-9edf-7bae56f1403b/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00002.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

## **Riches Beyond the Greek Roman Axis**

Until recently, any discussions of the rise of civilizations focused on the Greek-Roman axis — a reference point that ignored and undervalued the contributions of what is now Egypt and much of North Africa. In today’s world, many more liberal thinkers have stepped back to reject the idea of one culture [or religion] being the best.

Instead we look at the Mediterranean region as an extraordinary meshing of outstanding art and treasures and an invitation to the 21st century world of unleashed creativity and possibility — a wardrobe of beauty and innovation inspired by diversity. Built into this vision of humanity and civilization is its accompanying rejection of singularity of thought and lifestyle.

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/9e8a97b2-10f4-4c0d-b5d1-dec0094a9a90/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00003.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

### **Mediterranea Collections Triad: “Southern Radiance”; “Roman Splendor”; “East Meets West”**

Mediterranea was conceived in a triad of design inputs. The three creative universes, each reference a specific constellation of symbols, atmospheres, and inspirations.

The Bulgari *Mediterranea* universe called “Southern Radiance” alludes to the rich cultural legacy of southern Italy; “Roman Splendor” evokes the magnificence and mythology of the Eternal City of Rome; and “East Meets West” embodies the crossroads that is the Mediterranean Sea.

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/51532349-0ddb-4bec-994d-d09d41507734/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00004.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

> With Mediterranea, Bulgari continues its tradition of eclectic experimentation giving life to a kaleidoscopic collection of jewelry. “With great honor we celebrate the vision of the founder Sotirio Bulgari with magnificent creations that represent the pinnacle of Bulgari identity made of audacious creativity and exceptional craftsmanship,” says Bulgari CEO Jean-Christophe Babin.

Sotirio Bulgari [aka Sotirios Voulgaris 1857-1932] was born in the Greek village of Kalarites. Sotirios began his career as a jeweller in his home town of Paramythia (Epirus, Greece) and was a victim of war and conflict who eventually made his way to Corfu and then on to Naples, Italy.

Once in Italy, Sotirio’s name changed to Bulgari. Bulgari founded his eponymous jewelry company in 1884 on Via dei Condotti.

[![](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/55f45174e4b0fb5d95b07f39/71255c90-f550-483b-8e05-ff65636590cf/Bulgari-Mediterranea-May-2023-by-Gregoire-Alexandre-V+Magazine-142-00006.jpg)](https://anneofcarversville.com/jewelry-news/2023/5/26/bulgari-mediterranea-high-jewelry)

Anne learned a new word today — **syncretism**— to describe the goals of the Mediterranea collection. In my world of design, I’ve always called it cultural fusion — which is different from cultural appropriation or cultural assimilation.

With design employing syncretism, diverse cultural influences are obvious in the new design piece or work of art.

The colourful cultures and rich history of the Mediterranean are realised in some of the most exceptional jewellery creations from Bulgari yet, as Tatler Singapore discovers at the unveiling of the house’s latest high jewellery collection in Venice

After days of rain, the skies had cleared and the sun was out in all its glory on a beautiful day in May when I arrived in [Venice](https://www.tatlerasia.com/style/jewellery/emma-chamberlain-cartier-necklace-venice-film-festival-2022) for the launch of Bulgari’s latest high jewellery collection, Mediterranea.

Famously known as “The Floating City”, Venice is built on 118 small islands, connected by hundreds of bridges over the winding canals that characterise this charming northeast Italian city.

Throughout its history in the Middle Ages and the Renaissance period, Venice was a major maritime power thanks to its prime geographical position that allowed it to dominate the trade routes on the Mediterranean Sea and act as the key middleman between the Middle East and the Byzantine Empire. As the crossroads of cultures and Mediterranean influences that has served as a stage for countless meetings and exchanges over the centuries, it is no wonder that Venice was chosen as the picturesque setting for the glamorous event.

The theme of the collection was inspired by founder Sotirio Bulgari’s journey from his homeland of Greece through the Mediterranean before finally settling in Rome, Italy, where he founded his eponymous brand in 1884. His descendants later referenced this journey through jewellery creations that mixed Greek, Italian and Middle Eastern inspirations, which became Bulgari’s signature.

Mediterranea showcases the Roman jeweller’s unparalleled high jewellery craftsmanship and bold creativity by tracing a similar voyage across the Mediterranean. The collection is divided into three sub‑themes: Southern Radiance, which evokes the flamboyance and vibrancy of southern Italy; Roman Splendor, which pays homage to Bulgari’s roots in The Eternal City; and East Meets West, which touches on the various cultures that come together along the Mediterranean Sea from Europe, Africa and Asia. Together, they present an enthralling blend of Mediterranean inspirations connecting Eastern and Western cultures, Byzantine and Roman influences, and references to colourful North African and southern Italian Baroque beauty.

#### Magnificent Mediterranean

As befitting the splendid creations, Bulgari’s Mediterranea collection was unveiled to an exclusive group of media, including Tatler Singapore, and VIPs invited from around the world with Venice as the awe‑inspiring backdrop. Such grand‑scale events are an annual occurrence for the brand, which launches a new high jewellery collection, typically in a different city, each year. But many, such as Mauro Di Roberto, managing director of Bulgari’s jewellery business unit, deem it “the best [Bulgari] has ever done”.

On the morning of the launch, a light rain returned but fortunately stopped just before sunset, leaving the streets of Venice softly aglow with reflections of lights from surrounding boats and docks. As popular a tourist destination as it is—especially in summer—Venice’s lack of roads makes it a lot quieter than most cities, and allows for a perpetual sense of calm and romance, especially as night falls.

To the sound of water lapping in the canals and echoing through the narrow alleyways, or calli in Italian, we made our way to the jewellery show and gala dinner venue, keen to savour the dreamy atmosphere; hastening our steps as the temperature dropped and the moon started to peek out from behind the clouds. In a few minutes, we arrived at our magnificent destination—the city’s storied Palazzo Ducale—where our magical evening with Bulgari began.

Stepping into the grand, Gothic‑style palace in Piazza San Marco that overlooks the lagoon was an experience in itself; Palazzo Ducale is a sight to behold with its colonnades and marble arches—certainly a fitting former residence of the Doge of Venice, the main elected leader of the Venetian Republic.

We were seated along the length of the palace’s courtyard‑facing balcony, or loggia, for the private show, together with celebrities and Bulgari’s brand ambassadors, Lisa of K‑pop group Blackpink, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Liu Yifei, Hikari Mori and Yang Yang.

The stars were, of course, decked out in Bulgari jewels. Hathaway dazzled in a stunning necklace from the new collection, made in pink gold and set with six oval cabochon pink tourmalines surrounded by diamonds. Fellow Hollywood actress Zendaya, who often wears Serpenti creations, did not disappoint in an off‑shoulder gown that showed off the bold Serpenti piece around her neck, crafted in white gold and set with yellow diamonds, white diamonds and emeralds.

#### Eternal Beauty

On an exquisite mosaic runway, hand‑crafted in hues of the Mediterranean by traditional Venetian glass manufacturer Orsoni Venezia 1888 for the event, models, including Stella Maxwell, Blesnya Minher and Eva Herzigová, strutted out to the swells of the orchestral soundtrack created by Italian orchestra conductor Beatrice Venezi, showcasing more than 400 high jewellery masterpieces. Herzigová closed the show wearing one of the star creations from the new collection: the Muse of Rome white gold necklace fully decked in emeralds and diamonds, and  bearing a jaw‑dropping 218.53‑carat sugarloaf Colombian emerald at its centre. Thanks to a unique structure that allows the central sugarloaf emerald pendant to be detached, the necklace can be worn with or without the central stone, and also comes with an additional emerald bead and South Sea pearl sautoir that the pendant can be worn on.

It is a masterpiece that Di Roberto believes encapsulates the complexities of Bulgari’s craftsmanship expertise. “This is a unique stone not only because it’s huge, but more because it’s cut in such a way—cabochon sugarloaf, a typical cut representing Bulgari’s DNA—with a beautiful colour and quality as well as few inclusions,” he says. “The best way to emphasise the beauty of this stone is to mount it as we’ve done, and to keep it as clean and free as possible. When we frame it this way, we maximise the beauty and the radiance of the colour of the stone. To me, that’s an important sign of maturity when it comes to creating a product; not to overdo it.”

Tatler Singapore's Annabel Tan reports on the star-studded launch of Bulgari's Mediterranea high jewellery collection, unveiled in Venice in May 2023. The event took place at the historic Palazzo Ducale (a Gothic-style palace overlooking the lagoon, former residence of the Doge of Venice) for an exclusive group of media and VIPs, and featured a private runway show and gala dinner.

The collection is inspired by founder Sotirio Bulgari's journey from Greece through the Mediterranean to Rome, where he founded the brand in 1884. Mediterranea is divided into three sub-themes: Southern Radiance (evoking southern Italy's vibrancy), Roman Splendor (paying homage to Bulgari's Roman roots), and East Meets West (connecting European, African, and Asian cultures along the Mediterranean).

Celebrity attendees and brand ambassadors included Lisa of K-pop group Blackpink, Anne Hathaway, Zendaya, Priyanka Chopra Jonas, Liu Yifei, Hikari Mori, and Yang Yang. Hathaway wore a pink gold necklace set with six oval cabochon pink tourmalines surrounded by diamonds; Zendaya wore a bold Serpenti piece in white gold set with yellow diamonds, white diamonds, and emeralds.

The show featured more than 400 high jewellery masterpieces on a mosaic runway hand-crafted by traditional Venetian glass manufacturer Orsoni Venezia 1888, with an orchestral soundtrack conducted by Beatrice Venezi. Models included Stella Maxwell, Blesnya Minher, and Eva Herzigová, who closed the show wearing the Muse of Rome necklace — a white gold piece fully decked in emeralds and diamonds with a detachable 218.53-carat sugarloaf Colombian emerald at its centre, plus an additional emerald bead and South Sea pearl sautoir.

The next day, a private exhibition was held at Palazzo Soranzo Van Axel, a 15th-century Gothic palace, with each of the three sub-theme spaces decorated in collaboration with Venetian textile company Rubelli and featuring work by glassmaker Venini and its artistic director Marco Piva, including a blue modular glass sculpture inspired by the brand's Tazebao chandelier.

Bulgari managing director of the jewellery business unit, Mauro Di Roberto, called the event "the best [Bulgari] has ever done," and praised the Muse of Rome's sugarloaf cut as representing "Bulgari's DNA" with its clean, uncluttered framing that "maximises the beauty and the radiance of the colour of the stone." Another notable piece highlighted is the Mediterranean Muse necklace, featuring aquamarines, sapphires, and diamonds in a dynamic drop layout evoking undulating waves.

# Sea of Wonder: Celebrating the Ocean’s Endless Bounty with the Tiffany & Co. Blue Book 2025

June 16, 2025

9 min read

*Let's begin to explore this summer season's selection of exquisite high jewellery pieces with a collection that evokes dreams of gorgeous seaside resorts. The Tiffany & Co. new Blue Book chapter launched in 2025 is aptly called 'Sea of Wonder', taking us into a serene marine world that's perfectly infused with diamonds and coloured gemstones. Here are some of the creations that became an integral part of the Tiffany & Co. underwater world, including starfish, crashing waves and sea turtles…*

Through the language of jewellery, the brand's Chief Artistic Officer, Nathalie Verdeille, is taking high jewellery lovers on a journey through the mysterious ocean depths, drawing her key inspirations from the archive works of the legendary designer [Jean Schlumberger](https://www.katerinaperez.com/articles/top-5-designers-tiffany-co-history-schlumberger-picasso). Before we move to the review of the latest jewels, let's quickly delve into the past and discover the story of this extraordinary artist.

The French designer was born in Alsace, France, in 1907 into a family of textile manufacturers. The most obvious career choice for him would have been to continue in the family business. However, young Schlumberger was fascinated with drawing and became determined to forge [his own artistic path](https://www.katerinaperez.com/articles/historical-jewellers-with-distinctive-style). In his early twenties, he went to Paris, where he first worked for the French couturier Lucien Lelong and then for an art publisher. He dived into the vibrant, hedonistic, and rebellious art life of the city, which was full of new ideas and cultural influences.

![Jean Michel Schlumberger (1907-1987)](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Jean-Michel-Schlumberger.jpg)

Jean Michel Schlumberger (1907-1987)

There, Schlumberger started creating fashion jewellery using antique fragments, corals, shells, cameos, and porcelain flowers. They were extremely popular among members of the bohème. One day, a pair of his earrings worn by Princess Marina, Duchess of Kent, caught the eye of the famous couturier Elsa Schiaparelli, who subsequently commissioned Schlumberger to create fantasy buttons for her collections, the most notable of which was a flying acrobat concept for the 1938 Circus Collection. Having masterfully completed the commission, Schlumberger joined the list of acclaimed artists who worked for Schiaparelli, along with Salvador Dali, Jean Cocteau, and Louis Aragon. These surrealist jewellery pieces gave rise to the so-called “bijoux fantaisie” (fashion jewellery).

![Jean Schlumberger for Schiaparelli, Ostrich dress clips for the Circus collection, Summer 1938](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Jean-Schlumberger-for-Schiaparelli-Ostrich-dress-clips-summer-1938-for-the-Circus-collection.jpg)

Jean Schlumberger for Schiaparelli, Ostrich dress clips for the Circus collection, Summer 1938

Through the collaboration with Schiaparelli, Schlumberger became known worldwide, especially in the United States, but his career was interrupted by the events of World War II and military service. It was not until 1946 that he opened a small boutique on East 63rd Street in New York City together with his childhood friend Nicolas Bongard. Schlumberger coined his own signature style, bringing movement, life, colour and emotion to jewellery. His pieces were infused with deep meaning based on historical and cultural references; he also brought back yellow gold and bright enamels. This approach made him incredibly popular among connoisseur clients from high society.

![The desk of Jean Schlumberger, courtesy of Vanity Fair](/_ipx/s_571x762/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/5.-schlumberger_Source-Vanity-Fair.jpg)

The desk of Jean Schlumberger, courtesy of Vanity Fair

In 1956, the talented French jewellery designer Jean Schlumberger was invited to meet Walter Hoving, chairman of Tiffany & Co. He was offered access to a fascinating treasure trove of precious stones and complete freedom to create fantastic masterpieces. It was a milestone for both parties – Schlumberger became a designer for Tiffany & Co., and the company, in turn, started implementing an entirely new business model for the rapidly changing post-war world. It included combining the brand's heritage with the modernity, innovation and uniqueness of Schlumberger's creative vision.

![Tiffany & Co. Urchin necklace with a fancy intense yellow diamond of over 18 carats set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, surrounded by yellow and white diamonds, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-yellow-diamond-necklace.jpg)
![Tiffany & Co. Urchin ring with a fancy intense yellow diamond of over 9 carats set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, surrounded by white diamonds, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-yellow-diamond-ring.jpg)
![Tiffany & Co. Urchin earrings with fancy intense yellow diamonds weighing over 4 carats total set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, surrounded by yellow and white diamonds, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-earrings-yellow-diamonds-2.jpg)
![Tiffany & Co. Urchin ring with a fancy intense yellow diamond weighing over 12 carats set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, surrounded by white diamonds, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-yellow-diamonds-ring.jpg)
![Tiffany & Co. Urchin earrings with fancy intense yellow diamonds weighing over 2 carats total set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, surrounded by yellow and white diamonds, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-earrings-yellow-diamonds.jpg)

In collaboration with Tiffany & Co., he presented his own perceptions of nature, including a less literal depiction of earthly wonders – fish, flowers, birds, plants and trees. He frequently travelled to Bali, India, Thailand and Guadeloupe, where he was drawing, sketching and painting, inspired by the world around him and passionate about the sea. Schlumberger created jewellery and objects in the form of sea urchins, starfish, sea anemones and shells that were whimsical yet realistic. "I'm trying to show things growing unevenly, chaotically, organically, constantly in motion," he is quoted as saying. "I want to capture the irregularity of the universe."

![Tiffany & Co. Seahorse necklace with unenhanced purple sapphires of over 11 total carats, blue sapphires, moonstones and diamonds, set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Seahorse-necklace-sapphire-moonstone.jpg)

![Tiffany & Co. ![Tiffany & Co. Seahorse earrings with over 17 carats of blue zircons, sapphires, moonstones and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Seahorse-earrings.jpg)

Seahorse ring with a blue zircon over 10 carats, sapphires and diamonds in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Seahorse-ring.jpg)

In his work for Tiffany & Co., the designer always paid special attention to sketching to reflect the smallest details produced by his imagination. Drawings created by Schlumberger in the previous century come to life in the 2025 Sea of Wonder collection and feel incredibly fresh in Nathalie's new jewellery interpretation.

### Drawing inspiration from Jean Schlumberger’s fascination with the sea, our House’s pioneering spirit endures, driving us to reinvent archival inspirations from a modern perspective. – *Nathalie Verdeille*

The new collection and its 50 high jewellery pieces celebrate Schlumberger’s favourite sea creatures embodied in gold, platinum, diamonds and coloured gemstones. The collection is divided into several chapters, and I’d love to start with my favourite one – Seahorse, which features zircon as the main character. Unfortunately, this stone is often confused with cubic zirconia, which I [talked about on Instagram](https://www.instagram.com/reel/DIJKbobvZli/?utm_source=ig_web_copy_link&igsh=MzRlODBiNWFlZA==). In this chapter, it stands out against the background of moonstones, diamonds and sapphires. The highlights of Seahorse are a bib necklace and a brooch inspired by Jean Schlumberger’s famous seahorse brooch from 1968. New designs, such as a necklace with over 80 carats of blue zircons, elevate the original motif of flowing gold ‘ribbons’ into something more abstract and contemporary.

![Tiffany & Co. Seahorse brooch with blue zircons of over 12 carats, sapphires, moonstones and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Seahorse-brooch.jpg)

Tiffany & Co. Seahorse brooch with blue zircons of over 12 carats, sapphires, moonstones and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection

The Starfish pieces are inspired by a diamond and pearl brooch created by Jean Schlumberger in 1956, during his first year at Tiffany & Co. Today’s interpretation beautifully reimagines the original piece in a variety of textured silhouettes, including platinum and 18k yellow gold earrings set with over 4 carats of untreated rubies, a ring with a similar 6-carat stone, and a necklace with a transformable pendant that can be worn as a brooch.

![Tiffany & Co. Starfish ring with an unenhanced ruby of over 6 carats and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Starfish-ruby-ring.jpg)

Tiffany & Co. Starfish ring with an unenhanced ruby of over 6 carats and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection

### The rubies that we acquired for the Starfish chapter possess this gemstone’s most sought-after qualities: a strongly saturated red colour with a splash of fluorescence that is further enhanced by their high clarity. The unenhanced nature of these gemstones, coupled with the perfectly matched red colour and cut, is extremely rare. They are complemented by rose-cut and round brilliant diamonds that add a bit of antique inspiration with a modern twist. – *Tiffany & Co’s Chief Gemmologist, Victoria Wirth Reynolds*

The Urchin chapter draws inspiration from the intricately twisted gold ‘rope’ – a signature element of Schlumberger’s designs – and the sea urchin, first introduced as part of an iconic 1960s table clock. This chapter is an ode to yellow diamonds, as they adorn most of the jewels: the necklace features a central yellow diamond of over 18 carats, while the rings boast 12 and 9 carats. Three Urchin jewels are also decorated with paillonné enamel, a 19th-century technique revived by Jean Schlumberger, which adds contrast to the designs while simultaneously mimicking the iridescent essence of the sea.

![Tiffany & Co. Urchin earrings with fancy intense yellow diamonds of over 4 carats total, surrounded by yellow and white diamond accents and set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Urchin-earrings-yellow-diamond.jpg)

Tiffany & Co. Urchin earrings with fancy intense yellow diamonds of over 4 carats total, surrounded by yellow and white diamond accents and set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection

![Tiffany & Co. Bioluminescence Wave necklace with green cuprian elbaite tourmalines of over 10 total carats, blue cuprian elbaite tourmalines of over 6 total carats and diamonds set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Wave-diamond-necklace-tourmalines.jpg)

The Wave chapter celebrates the dramatic movement of the ocean with voluminous diamond jewels featuring green and blue cuprian elbaite tourmalines. For example, the spectacular articulated necklace is set with diamonds to highlight the electric hues of over 17 carats of blue and green elbaite tourmalines. The piece is inspired by the voluminous shapes and dynamic movement first used in Schlumberger’s famous Leaves necklace in 1956. It is complemented by several earring and ring options featuring the same stones. For those who prefer a monochrome palette, there are several pieces with colourless diamonds. By the way, you’ve probably already seen Natalie Portman wearing the necklace on [the red carpet at the Cannes Film Festival](https://www.katerinaperez.com/articles/best-cannes-jewellery).

![Tiffany & Co. Bioluminescence Wave earrings with blue cuprian elbaite tourmaline of over 2 carats, green cuprian elbaite tourmalines of over 2 total carats and diamonds set in 18k white and yellow gold, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/s_1000x1333/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Wave-earring.jpg)

Tiffany & Co. Bioluminescence Wave earrings with blue cuprian elbaite tourmaline of over 2 carats, green cuprian elbaite tourmalines of over 2 total carats and diamonds set in 18k white and yellow gold, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection

Of course, the collection introduces some new motifs. The ocean comes alive in the Ocean Flora chapter, blooming with fantastic sea plants. The necklace brings together five exclusively selected unenhanced Zambian emeralds totalling more than 10 carats. Elsewhere, the Sea Turtle chapter combines sophisticated diamond-studded patterns with intricate gold detailing. A standout design, the Sea Turtle pendant features a cushion-cut diamond weighing over 4 carats and has a hidden mechanism that transforms the piece into a brooch, reflecting the turtle’s journey from land to sea. Just imagine that it took over 900 hours to create!

![Tiffany & Co. Sea Turtle diamond pendant-brooch with a diamond of over 4 carats, sapphires and further diamonds set in platinum and 18k yellow gold, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/s_1000x1332/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Sea-Turtle-diamond-brooch.jpg)

Tiffany & Co. Sea Turtle diamond pendant-brooch with a diamond of over 4 carats, sapphires and further diamonds set in platinum and 18k yellow gold, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection

### The expertise of our craftspeople is especially evident in the Sea Turtle chapter, where the turtle’s geometric, graphic shell is adorned with hexagons, each formed by 24 delicately hand-engraved petals. Each piece demands more than 550 hours of meticulous craftsmanship, resulting in hypnotic volume and texture. – *Nathalie Verdeille*

Through the language of jewellery, the brand’s Chief Artistic Officer, Nathalie Verdeille, is taking high jewellery lovers on a journey through the mysterious ocean depths, drawing her key inspirations from the archive works of the legendary designer [Jean Schlumberger](https://www.katerinaperez.com/articles/top-5-designers-tiffany-co-history-schlumberger-picasso). Before we move to the review of the latest jewels, let’s quickly delve into the past and discover the story of this extraordinary artist.

![Tiffany & Co. Sea Turtle earrings with diamonds of over 3 total carats and further diamond accents set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-golden-earrings.jpg)
![Tiffany & Co. Sea Turtle ring with a diamond of over 2 carats and further diamond accents set in 18k yellow gold and platinum, from the Sea of Wonder Blue Book 2025 High Jewellery collection](/_ipx/f_webp&q_80/https://api.katerinaperez.com/wp-content/uploads/Tiffany-Co.-Blue-Book-2025-Sea-of-Wonder-Sea-Turtle-golden-ring.jpg)

The Blue Book 2025: Sea of Wonder reimagines the hidden wonders of the ocean and reminds us that the most beautiful things in the world are often to be found in the most unexplored places. This collection is a testament to Tiffany & Co.'s commitment to creativity, craftsmanship, and a deep appreciation for nature's endless mysteries.
